## The question

[Easier way to enable verbose logging](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14097061/easier-way-to-enable-verbose-logging), asked by [user1934146](https://stackoverflow.com/users/1934146/user1934146) on Stack Overflow (2012-12-31; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I want to add a debug print statement test, if I enable `--verbose` from the command line and if I have the following in the script.
>
> ```python
> logger.info("test")
> ```
>
> I went through the following questions, but couldn't get the answer...
>
> - https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5980042/how-to-implement-the-verbose-or-v-option-into-a-python-script
>
> - https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9042919/python-logging-is-there-something-below-debug
:::

I find both `--verbose` (for users) and `--debug` (for developers) useful.  Here's how I do it with `logging` and `argparse`:

```python
import argparse
import logging

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument(
    '-d', '--debug',
    help="Print lots of debugging statements",
    action="store_const", dest="loglevel", const=logging.DEBUG,
    default=logging.WARNING,
)
parser.add_argument(
    '-v', '--verbose',
    help="Be verbose",
    action="store_const", dest="loglevel", const=logging.INFO,
)
args = parser.parse_args()    
logging.basicConfig(level=args.loglevel)
```

So if `--debug` is set, the logging level is set to `DEBUG`.  If `--verbose`, logging is set to `INFO`.  If neither, the lack of `--debug` sets the logging level to the default of `WARNING`.
